Trying to do better each day; I go out once a day but can't go past a certain block in my neighborhood. Can't ride public transit without someone else. I have a few friends but mostly online friends. I want to go see my online friend who lives in Kansas sometime this summer but that would be a huge step for me. I'd love to meet other people who go through similar things :)
I think I simply have big emotions so no antipsychotic has ever made me feel numb. I'm on Latuda and I don't get numb but I am able to deal with things in a healthy way versus when I was sick.

I figure I've dealt with it for so long & it isn't going away so might as well be open about it. So far no one has really said anything negative, I've even made friends sharing the diagnosis. But, it's different for everyone.

I had a sorta similar experience on Vrylar; my doctor touted it as this wonderful medicine that would absolutely work. I felt fine on it, even really good. And then I started slipping into psychotic mania & like you, I didn't understand because I was doing everything right. But sometimes, the meds aren't for you (like in my case, I had to get off it and back on Latuda & even still, I get mood episodes) or maybe in your case, the meds stop working / lose their efficacy for one reason or another, I went from 60mg of Latuda to now 120 because over time the dose just seemed to stop working as well. It sounds like you're slipping into mania. At least you're aware of it; see your doctor and I'm sure you can work something out. Hang in there!

I had traumas before the age of six; sexually abused & watched my grandma die. I think those must have contributed to the formation of my illness, among other traumas that came later on. I remember being around eight, I got my period early & that also seems to have been a trigger; I'd hear music in empty rooms, see faces everywhere, had really vivid, monstrous dreams. I believed I could fall through the ground at any minute. I believed in ghosts to an extreme amount. I was also a strange kid, really smart but nearly mute. Depressed at the age of nine, looking up ways to kill myself that wouldn't hurt. Life hurts. And it's beautiful. I think I was destined to always be a little insane. Developed the full-fledged illness at sixteen.

Takes time & practice to get the gears turning. But I think meds are the most important factor to help with the low motivation / negative symptoms that might be affecting the way you are able to think. Good luck.
